## Overview

A snackbar is a brief, non-blocking message about something the app just did or could not do: "Booking confirmed", "Item removed from cart", "Payment failed". It appears at the bottom of the screen, it never takes focus, and it leaves on its own unless the user needs time to act. It can carry **one** action (Undo, Retry, View) and an optional close button.

Three variant axes drive it:

- **Appearance** is on trial. Both ship so the team can compare them in product:
  - **Inverse** is a near-black bar. Intent changes only the leading glyph and its colour. This is the Material and Human Interface pattern: a quiet, consistent surface that reads the same in every flow.
  - **Tinted** is a light intent surface with a matching border, closer to an inline banner. The intent reads from the surface, the border, the icon and the action.
- **Intent** sets the default glyph and the colours: Neutral, Info, Success, Caution, Warning. Warning means an error, following the Cosmos semantic naming, so it uses red.
- **Layout** covers two arrangements. `Inline` keeps the action beside the message. `Stacked` moves it to its own row, right-aligned, for labels too long to sit inline ("Try another method").

### When to use something else

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| The message must stay until the user acts on it, or blocks the task | Dialog |
| The message belongs to one section of the page, such as a form error or a fare rule | Inline banner or field error |
| The message is persistent page state, such as offline mode or a maintenance notice | Page-level banner |
| The feedback is a single control changing state | The control itself, for example a Button loading state |

### Composition

- **Snackbar / Control** (constitutive: set `636:3088`, 48 variants of Type × Tone × State) holds the action and close buttons. It is nested in every Snackbar variant with the Tone that matches, and exposed, so its `State` and `Label` can be set from the Snackbar panel. It was created for this component.
- **Icon / check** (referenced: `55:14`) is the Neutral glyph.
- **Icon / info** (`635:120`), **Icon / check-circle** (`635:123`), **Icon / alert-triangle** (`635:126`) and **Icon / alert-circle** (`635:129`) are referenced status glyphs, created for this component. Like every Cosmos glyph they live on the Figma **Icons** page (`645:2`) and are Material Symbols Rounded (`info`, `check_circle`, `warning`, `error`) at weight 300, grade 0, optical size 24 (Apache 2.0). Outside a component, use the Icon container set (`645:28`), which swaps glyphs and sizes them to the `icon.*` tokens.
- **Icon / close** (referenced: `55:17`) is the close glyph.
- _Decorative children: 1 (Focus Ring, inside Snackbar / Control). It is documented under Structure._

## API

> `Appearance` is a trial axis, not a permanent product choice. Build both, and expect one to be retired.
>
> `State` on Snackbar / Control is design-only. `Hover`, `Pressed` and `Focus` exist so a mock can show them. In code they are `:hover`, `:active` and `:focus-visible` on the action and close buttons. The snackbar container has no interaction states.

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | (string) | – | Required. One or two lines; see Behaviour. |
| `title` | string | (string) | `none` | A bold line above the message, for richer web toasts. Keep it under about 40 characters. |
| `appearance` | enum | inverse \| tinted | `inverse` | Trial axis. |
| `intent` | enum | neutral \| info \| success \| caution \| warning | `neutral` | Sets the default glyph and the colours. Warning means an error. |
| `icon` | icon \| false | (icon) | per intent | Defaults to the intent glyph. Pass `false` to hide it; the Neutral glyph is often dropped. The icon is decorative, because the message carries the meaning. |
| `action` | `{ label, onAction }` | (object) | `none` | One action at most. Tapping it also dismisses the snackbar with reason `action`. Never "Dismiss" or "OK"; use `showClose` instead. |
| `showClose` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Adds a close button. Required when `duration` is `indefinite`. |
| `duration` | enum \| ms | short \| long \| indefinite \| (number) | `short` | short = 4 s, long = 7 s. Any snackbar with an action is at least `long`, and becomes `indefinite` while a screen reader is running. See Behaviour. |
| `layout` | enum | auto \| inline \| stacked | `auto` | `auto` stacks when the action label would squeeze the message below about 60% of the width, or would wrap. |
| `placement` | enum | bottom \| bottom-start \| bottom-center | `bottom` | Mobile: bottom, full width minus margins. Web: bottom-center on narrow viewports, bottom-start on wide layouts with a side navigation. |
| `onDismiss` | callback | `(reason) => void` | – | reason: `timeout`, `action`, `close`, `swipe`, `escape`, `replaced` or `programmatic`. |

### Figma-only properties

| Figma property | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Show icon` | BOOLEAN | `true` | |
| `Show title` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Title` | TEXT | `"Title"` | Placeholder copy. |
| `Message` | TEXT | `"Message"` | Placeholder copy, the same in every variant. |
| `Show action` | BOOLEAN | `true` | In Stacked it hides the whole action row. |
| `Show close` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Action` | Nested instance | `State=Default` | Exposed. Set its `Label` (placeholder `"Action"`) and `State` (Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus) from the Snackbar panel. |
| `Close` | Nested instance | `State=Default` | Exposed, so its `State` can be mocked. |

Every variant ships placeholder copy only (Title, Message, Action), so no sample sentence is mistaken for approved product copy. Realistic copy lives in the `Snackbar examples` frame. There is no `Leading icon` swap property, because a set-level default would reset every intent to one glyph. Swap the glyph on the layer instead.

### Examples

| # | Configuration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `message="Item removed from cart"`, `action={label:"Undo"}`, `icon=false` | The classic undo snackbar. |
| 2 | `intent=success`, `title="Booking confirmed"`, `message="Booking ID MMT-4821 sent to your email."`, `showClose` | No action, so the close button gives manual control. |
| 3 | `intent=warning`, `message="Payment failed. No money was deducted."`, `action={label:"Retry"}` | Error with a recovery path. |
| 4 | `intent=caution`, `message="Only 2 rooms left at this price"`, `action={label:"Book"}` | Urgency nudge. Use sparingly. |
| 5 | `intent=info`, `layout=stacked`, `action={label:"Set a reminder"}`, `showClose` | Long action label on its own row. |

The Figma page has these as a live `Snackbar examples` frame (`637:3330`).

## Behaviour

- **One at a time.** Queue snackbars first in, first out. A new message waits for the current one to leave. The exception is a message that supersedes the current one, such as "Retrying…" after "Payment failed"; that replaces it at once with reason `replaced`.
- **Timing.**

  | Content | Duration |
  |---|---|
  | Message only | 4 s |
  | Message with an action, or more than about 12 words | 7 s |
  | Screen reader running and an action present | Indefinite; the close button is required |

  Android's `AccessibilityManager.getRecommendedTimeoutMillis` and the iOS equivalent (`UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning`) decide the last row. That row satisfies WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable.
- **Pausing.** The timer pauses while the pointer is over the snackbar or focus is inside it (web), and while a finger is on it (mobile). It restarts from the full duration when the pause ends.
- **Dismissal.** Dismissal happens:
  - on timeout
  - when the action is activated
  - when the close button is pressed
  - on a horizontal swipe on mobile
  - on Escape on web, while focus is inside the snackbar or the snackbar is the most recent one
- **Focus.** The snackbar never moves focus when it appears. The action is reachable by keyboard: on web, add it to the tab order at the end of the page region, or bind F6 to reach the live region. After dismissal, focus returns to where it was, if it had moved into the snackbar.
- **Placement.** Stay above bottom navigation, a floating action button and the home indicator. Respect the safe area, with an inset of `snackbar/margin-mobile` (16) or `snackbar/margin-desktop` (24). On mobile the snackbar spans the width minus margins. On web it hugs content between 288 and 560 px wide.
- **Copy.** Keep the message to two lines. Write it in sentence case with no full stop on a single sentence. Keep the action to one or two words where possible, in title case per MakeMyTrip button copy.

### Motion

| Phase | Movement | Duration | Easing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | Slide up 16 px and fade 0 → 1 | `snackbar/enter-duration` (`duration.lg`) | `snackbar/easing` (`easing.standard`) |
| Exit | Fade 1 → 0 (with swipe: follow the finger, then fade) | `duration.md`, one size down from the entrance | `easing.standard` |
| Replace | Exit the old one, then enter the new one | Exit, then enter | as above |

With `prefers-reduced-motion`, or Reduce Motion on iOS and Android, use the fade alone with no slide. On the web the entrance is a transition started with `@starting-style`; the exit is not built yet (see Known gaps).

## Structure

### Anatomy

```text
Snackbar (component set · 637:3233) · Layout=Inline · item spacing gap-controls
├─ Content (frame · horizontal · fill width · end padding content-padding-end)
│  ├─ Leading icon (instance · Icon / info …) · a11y-hidden · Show icon
│  └─ Text (frame · vertical · fill width)
│     ├─ Title (text · title/small/bold) · Show title, hidden by default
│     └─ Message (text · body/medium/regular)
├─ Action (instance · Snackbar / Control · Type=Action) · Show action · exposed
└─ Close (instance · Snackbar / Control · Type=Close) · Show close, hidden by default · exposed

Snackbar · Layout=Stacked
├─ Top row (frame · horizontal · top-aligned · item spacing gap-controls)
│  ├─ Content (frame · horizontal · top-aligned · fill width · top padding content-padding-top-stacked · end padding content-padding-end)
│  │  ├─ Leading icon
│  │  └─ Text (Title, Message)
│  └─ Close
└─ Actions (frame · horizontal · right-aligned) · Show action
   └─ Action

Snackbar / Control (component set · 636:3088)
├─ Focus Ring (rectangle) · decorative · absolute, 4 px outside, stretches with the button · visible only at State=Focus
└─ Label (text · label/medium/bold)  — Type=Action
   or Icon (instance · Icon / close)  — Type=Close
```

Both layouts hug their content vertically: the snackbar never drops below `snackbar/min-height` (48), and it grows by 20 px for each extra message line and by 20 px for the title (its line, with `snackbar/gap-text` at 0). Controls never share a wrapper frame. In Inline, Action and Close are direct children of the snackbar; in Stacked, Close sits beside Content in the top row. A hidden control therefore leaves no gap and the text fills the row. Two Figma booleans cannot hide a shared parent when both are off. In both layouts the spacing works out as follows:

| Controls shown | Text to first control | Action to close | Text to edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| None beside the text | – | – | 16 (`content-padding-end` 4 + `padding-end-control` 12) |
| Action and/or close (Inline), or close (Stacked) | 12 (`content-padding-end` 4 + `gap-controls` 8) | 8 (Inline) | – |

Items are centred on the cross axis, so the 24 px icon and the controls sit mid-height beside a message of any length. In Stacked, the content row is top-aligned: the 24 px icon starts level with the first text line and overhangs its 20 px line box by 4 px below.

### Dimensions

The same in every Appearance and Intent.

| Property | Value | Token |
|---|---|---|
| Min height | 48; hugs content above that | `snackbar/min-height` |
| Width | Mobile: screen minus 2 × 16. Web: 288 to 560, hugging content. Figma mocks: 360. | not tokenised |
| Padding start | 16 | `snackbar/padding-x` |
| Padding end (right), both layouts | 12 | `snackbar/padding-end-control` |
| Padding top and bottom, Inline | 8 | `snackbar/padding-y` |
| Padding top, Stacked | 8 to the close button, 12 to the icon and text | `snackbar/padding-y` + `snackbar/content-padding-top-stacked` (4) |
| Padding bottom, Stacked | 8 | `snackbar/padding-y` |
| Gap: icon to text | 12 | `snackbar/gap` |
| Gap: text to first control | 12 | `snackbar/content-padding-end` (4) + `snackbar/gap-controls` (8) |
| Gap: title to message | 0 | `snackbar/gap-text` |
| Gap: action to close | 8 | `snackbar/gap-controls` |
| Gap: text to action row, Stacked | 8 | `snackbar/stacked-gap` |
| Leading icon | 24 | `snackbar/icon-size` |
| Title type | 14 / 20 bold | `title/small/bold` |
| Message type | 14 / 20 regular | `body/medium/regular` |
| Corner radius | 12 | `snackbar/radius` |
| Border width, Tinted only | 1 | `snackbar/border-width` |
| Shadow | 0 1 2 and 0 2 6, neutral 950 | `shadow.card` (effect style `shadow/card`) |
| Action height | 32 | `snackbar/control-height` |
| Action padding x | 8 | `snackbar/control-padding-x` |
| Action type | 14 / 20 bold | `label/medium/bold` |
| Close button | 32 × 32 | `snackbar/close-size` |
| Close glyph | 20 | `snackbar/close-icon-size` |
| Control radius | 8 | `snackbar/control-radius` |
| Control hit area | 48 × 48 minimum | `snackbar/min-touch-target` |
| Focus ring | 2 px, 2 px outside, radius 12 | `snackbar/focus-ring-width`, `snackbar/focus-ring-offset`, `snackbar/focus-ring-radius` |
| Screen margin | 16 mobile, 24 web | `snackbar/margin-mobile`, `snackbar/margin-desktop` |

Inline padding is 8 so that 8 + 32 px action + 8 lands exactly on the 48 px min height. A one-line message without an action is also 48 tall, held by the min height, and each extra line adds 20 (two lines: 56). Every variant keeps 12 on the right, where the action or close button meets the edge; the text block adds 4 of its own, so with no control beside it the text still ends 16 from the edge, matching the left. Stacked puts the 32 px close button 8 from the top and 12 from the right; the icon and text drop a further 4 to start 12 from the top. Below the action row it keeps 8, because the 32 px button already carries its own inner space.

## Color

Token names follow `snackbar/{property}-{appearance}-{intent}[-{state}]`. Control tokens on Inverse drop the intent, because the dark bar is the same for every intent. `State=Focus` uses the `default` colours and adds the ring.

Every foreground has a same-suffix `bg-*` token, even where the value repeats (for example, five identical `bg-inverse-*`). This lets the `tokens/contrast` lint check each label and icon against the surface it actually sits on.

### Container — `snackbar/bg-*`, `snackbar/border-*`, `snackbar/label-*`, `snackbar/icon-*`

| Intent | Inverse fill | Inverse icon | Tinted fill | Tinted border | Tinted icon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Neutral | `bg-fill-inverse` #0A0A0A | `icon-inverse` #FFFFFF | `bg-surface-secondary` #FFFFFF | `border` #D4D4D4 | `icon` #0A0A0A |
| Info | `bg-fill-inverse` | `icon-info-inverse` #48BBFF | `bg-surface-info` #EDFAFF | `border-info` #83DFFF | `icon-info` #0088FF |
| Success | `bg-fill-inverse` | `icon-success-inverse` #05DF72 | `bg-surface-success` #F0FDF4 | `border-success` #7BF1A8 | `icon-success` #008236 |
| Caution | `bg-fill-inverse` | `icon-caution-inverse` #FDC700 | `bg-surface-caution` #FEFCE8 | `border-caution` #FFDF20 | `icon-caution` #A65F00 |
| Warning | `bg-fill-inverse` | `icon-warning-inverse` #FF6467 | `bg-surface-warning` #FEF2F2 | `border-warning` #FFA2A2 | `icon-warning` #C10007 |

Title and message use `text-inverse` (#FFFFFF) on Inverse and `text-primary` (#0A0A0A) on Tinted, for every intent. The Inverse appearance has no border.

### Action and close — `snackbar/bg-control-*`, `snackbar/label-control-*`, `snackbar/icon-control-*`

| Tone | Fill: default / hover / pressed | Action label: default / hover / pressed | Close glyph |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inverse | `bg-fill-inverse` / `bg-fill-inverse-hover` / `bg-fill-inverse-pressed` | `text-link-inverse` #83DFFF in all states | `icon-inverse-secondary` #A1A1A1 |
| Tinted Neutral | `bg-fill` / `bg-fill-brand-subtlest` / `bg-fill-brand-subtlest-hover` (the Text Button pattern) | `text-brand` / `text-brand-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` / `-pressed` | `icon-secondary` #525252 |
| Tinted Info | `bg-fill-info-subtlest` / `-hover` / `-pressed` | `text-info` / `text-info-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` / `-pressed` | `icon-secondary` |
| Tinted Success | `bg-fill-success-subtlest` / `-hover` / `-pressed` | `text-success` / `text-success-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` / `-pressed` | `icon-secondary` |
| Tinted Caution | `bg-fill-caution-subtlest` / `-hover` / `-pressed` | `text-caution` / `text-caution-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` / `-pressed` | `icon-secondary` |
| Tinted Warning | `bg-fill-warning-subtlest` / `-hover` / `-pressed` | `text-warning` / `text-warning-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` / `-pressed` | `icon-secondary` |

At rest, the control fill equals the snackbar fill, so the action reads as text. It is a real colour rather than transparent, so the lint can check the label against it. On Tinted, the action follows the intent colour and darkens one step on hover and press, as the Chip selected label does.

The focus ring is `snackbar/focus-ring` (`border-focus`, #0088FF) on both appearances.

This component added four semantic roles: **`color.icon-info-inverse`**, **`color.icon-success-inverse`**, **`color.icon-caution-inverse`** and **`color.icon-warning-inverse`**, all at step 400. The existing `icon-{intent}` roles are step 700. On near black success, caution and warning reach only 3.08 to 4.01:1 (info, on the lighter `azure.700`, reaches 5.62:1), with warning barely over the 3:1 floor, and they read as muddy. The 400 steps give 6.85 to 12.58:1. Reuse the new roles for any status glyph on a dark surface, such as a tooltip or a dark badge.

## Accessibility

### Contrast

| Pair | Ratio | Required | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inverse text #FFFFFF on #0A0A0A | 19.79:1 | 4.5:1 (1.4.3) | Pass |
| Inverse status icons on #0A0A0A (lowest: warning #FF6467) | 6.85:1 | 3:1 (1.4.11) | Pass |
| Inverse action #83DFFF on rest / hover / pressed | 13.16 / 11.92 / 10.06:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Inverse close #A1A1A1, lowest (on pressed #262626) | 5.85:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Tinted text #0A0A0A, lowest (on #FEF2F2) | 18.09:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Tinted status icons, lowest (info #0088FF on #EDFAFF) | 3.30:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Tinted action at rest, lowest (info #0088FF on #EDFAFF) | 3.30:1 | 3:1 (azure exception) | Pass |
| Tinted action at rest, lowest outside azure (success #008236 on #F0FDF4) | 4.72:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Tinted action hover, lowest (info #0868C5 on #D6F3FF) | 4.77:1 | 3:1 (azure exception) | Pass |
| Tinted action pressed, lowest (info #0D589B on #B5EAFF) | 5.60:1 | 3:1 (azure exception) | Pass |
| Tinted close #525252, lowest (on #FFC9C9) | 5.37:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Focus ring #0088FF on #0A0A0A / lowest tint (#FEF2F2) | 5.62 / 3.21:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Tinted border on its tint (lowest: caution) | 1.28:1 | – | Decorative; see below |

The Tinted border is decorative. The snackbar floats over content on the `shadow/card` shadow, and it is identified by its text, not its edge. So 1.4.11 does not require the boundary to reach 3:1, the same reasoning as the Chip border.

### Intent must not rely on colour alone

On the Inverse bar the icon is the only intent signal, and on Tinted the tint adds only a hue. Each intent therefore has a **different glyph shape**: tick, i, check in a circle, triangle, exclamation in a circle. The message must state the outcome in words ("Payment failed", not "Oops"). Hiding the icon is fine for Neutral, but on other intents it removes the non-text cue, and the copy must carry it.

### Semantics

| | Web | iOS / VoiceOver | Android / TalkBack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Announce | Render into a live region that exists before the message arrives: `role="status"` (`aria-live="polite"`) for Neutral, Info, Success and Caution; `role="alert"` (assertive) for Warning. Do not inject the region together with its text, because many screen readers miss it. | Post `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(message)` (SwiftUI) or `UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, …)`. Use `.isStaticText` on the text. | `accessibilityLiveRegion = POLITE` on the container (Compose: `Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }`); Material `SnackbarHost` does this. Warning may use `Assertive`. |
| Accessible text | Title, then message. The icon is `aria-hidden="true"`. | Title and message combined into one element. | Title and message merged; the icon has `contentDescription = null`. |
| Action | `<button>` with its visible label | Button trait; also offered as a custom action on the snackbar element | Clickable with `Role.Button`; Material also exposes it as a custom action |
| Close | `<button aria-label="Dismiss notification">` | Button, label "Dismiss" | `contentDescription = "Dismiss"` |
| Escape and back | Escape dismisses | The accessibility escape gesture (two-finger Z) dismisses | Back does **not** dismiss; it acts on the screen beneath |

**Focus order.** When focus is moved into the snackbar: action, then close. The snackbar never receives focus on its own.

**Touch target.** Action and close are 32 px tall visually. Expand their hit area in code to `snackbar/min-touch-target` (48) without changing the visible size, and do not let the two areas overlap. This is not modelled in Figma.

## Platform mapping

| | Android | iOS | Web |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | Material 3 `Snackbar` in a `SnackbarHost` (Compose) with a custom `snackbar` slot for Cosmos visuals | No native equivalent. Build a custom overlay: a view in a `ZStack` or an `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` above the tab bar, driven by a queue in an observable model | A single toast region component with a queue, mounted once near the root, positioned `fixed` bottom |
| Duration | `SnackbarDuration.Short` / `Long` / `Indefinite`, with the Cosmos timings above | Timer in the queue model | Timer in the queue, paused on hover and focus |
| Swipe | `SwipeToDismissBox` | `DragGesture`, horizontal | Pointer events on touch devices |

## Known gaps

- **Appearance is a trial.** Inverse and Tinted both ship. Once one is chosen, delete the other appearance tokens (about 50 of the 114), its Figma variants and its Control tones.
- **Exit is not animated on the web.** The snackbar unmounts as soon as it is dismissed, so the `duration.md` fade-out needs the component to stay mounted until the fade ends.
- **Web width is not tokenised.** 288 min and 560 max are beyond the space scale, which stops at 64. They are documented here only.
- **No leading icon swap property.** A set-level instance-swap default resets every intent to one glyph (tested and reverted), so the glyph is swapped on the layer.
- **`snackbar/focus-ring-offset` is not bound in Figma.** As on Chip, the 4 px outset is ring geometry. The ring binds width, radius and colour.
- **Queue, placement and live region are app-level.** No token covers the offset above bottom navigation; it depends on each screen.
- **No dark mode.** All variable collections are single-mode.
- **Not uSpec-generated.** This file is hand-authored next to the Figma build.
